newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Beobanka to restructure,welcomes foreign help.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Beobanka to restructure,welcomes foreign help.

text.p: Yugoslavia's largest commercial bank Beobanka reiterated on Thursday its commitment to become a bank tailored to European standards and said it welcomed foreign banks taking part in its restructuring.

Foreign banks can become Beobanka's partners by purchasing stake from its capitalisation issues or taking part in its further privatisation, Beobanka's general manager Zlatan Perucic told an annual shareholders meeting.

"Fields of cooperation are wide and different. They can join by giving credit support to best investment projects of Beobanka's clients, opening new credit lines, extending credits to Yugoslav companies doing business with foreigners.
"They can also mediate in the technology transfer or in launching new banking services," he said.

Perucic insisted Beobanka's restructuring was a part of its strategy for the rest of the century and will be conducted in line with a wider bank reconstruction programme, which Serbia's government is expected to present within few weeks.
He insisted banks would have to restructure on their own because state-coffers had no funds to compensate huge losses of the banking or the enterprise sector.
"If the state reduces its intervention to protect public interest, then it turns out the banking system must undertake reconstruction on its own," he said.
Bank privatisation and restructuring still waited for the Serbian privatisation ministry to ready a banking system reconstruction programme.
Perucic said Beobanka's restructuring will be discussed at an extraordinary shareholders meeting in May.

"We expect to mobilise all our available resources for strong and dynamic development of our bank that will strengthen its leading position and give big contribution to further economic development," Perucic said.
The bank reported 32.987 million dinars ($5.82 million) in gross profits for 1996, 32 million dinars of which will be set aside in a special risk-protection fund.
Shareholders agreed that instead of paying dividend, the remaining 987,000 dinars in profits will be transferred to the bank's reserves.

The final audited figures for the bank's 1995 and 1996 performance will be available late in May or early in June, Beobanka's spokesman Zoran Pavlovic told Reuters. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
